Course Descriptions
Courses not offered in the current academic year are sted at the end of this section.

courses.label: ANTH 101
courses.title: Human and Cultural Evolution
paras: An overview of Physical Anthropology and Archaeology. Lectures on living and fossil primates, the fossil evidence for the origins and development of man, modern races, and archaeological evidence for the origins and development of culture.

courses.label: ANTH 102A
courses.title: Introduction to Social and Cultural Anthropology
paras: The dynamic nature of socio-cultural systems is examined. Topics include language, technology, social organization, economics, politics, and religion. Data are drawn from a broad ethnographic base, including both “primitive” cultures and modem, developed societies.
A student may not take both ANTH 102A and ANTH 1028 for credit.

courses.label: ANTH 102B
courses.title: Anthropology Through Science Fiction
paras: Basic anthropolagical concepts, such as biological and cultural evolution, culture, human adaptability, and culture contact will be explored through examples from science fiction and related anthropological studies.

courses.label: ANTH 103
courses.title: The Nature of Language
paras: A general introduction to the scientific study of language. Lectures on the nature of human language as compared with animal communication, some of the basic methods of historical and descriptive linguistics, and the importance of language in culture and society.

courses.label: ANTH 201
courses.title: Principles of Archaeology
paras: An introduction to the working .assumptions, analytic approaches, and integrative and descriptive methods of archaediogical anthropology.

courses.label: ANTH 202
courses.title: Principles of Social Organization
paras: An introduction to. basic concepts used by social anthropologists for the analysis of social, economic, political and ideational systems.
Prereq: ANTH 102A or ANTH 1028 or permission of the instructor

courses.label: ANTH 203B
courses.title: North American Prehistory
paras: This is a general introduction to North American Archaeology. The traditional Cultural ecological approach is used.

courses.label: ANTH 222
courses.title: Prehistoric Cultures of the Great Lakes Area - A Survey
paras: A general survey of the archaeological evidence of prehistoric man in the Great Lakes area from his arrival ca. 11,000 years ago to the coming of the Europeans. Cultural ecology and cultural evolution will be stressed.
Honours Anthropology students should take ANTH 322.

courses.label: ANTH 224
courses.title: Archaeology and the Growth of
paras: Cultural Complexity

Archaeological approaches to cultural complexity are examined, using Newand Old World examples. Topics considered may include: agricultural Archaeological and ethnographic evidence concerning human adaptations over origins, megaliths, chiefdoms, states, and the emergence of cities, and early civilizations. Regional emphasis may vary.

courses.label: ANTH 228
courses.title: Peoples of the Pacific
paras: A comparative ethnological survey of selected indigenous societies in the Pacific Region.

courses.label: ANTH 230
courses.title: Indians of Canada The cultures of Canadian Indians are
paras: described as they existed when initially contacted by Europeans. Consideration i$ given to economic adaptation, social organization, political structure, material culture, ritual, and mythology.
Prereq: Second year standing

courses.label: ANTH 258
courses.title: Anthropology and the Future
paras: Anthropological theories pertaining to culture change and cultural evolution are examined in the context of the modern world. Long and short term trends in technology are examined using data from Archaeology, Ethnography, History, Technology and Science.
Prereq: ANTH 101 or 102 or permission of the instructor

courses.label: ANTH 260
courses.title: Human Evotution
paras: Data, methods, and theory in the study of the origin and evolution of humans are surveyed. Topics will include osteology, grawth and development, the fossil record, and genetics.
Prereq: ANTH 101 or permission of the instructor

courses.label: ANTH 261
courses.title: Primate Behaviour
paras: An introduction to the behaviour of nonhuman primates and its relevance to human development. Topics will include social organization, role behaviour, and communication patterns, as well as the history of primate studies.

courses.label: ANTH 270
courses.title: Archaeological Method and Techniques
paras: Survey of archaeological approaches to data focusing on field observation and recording. Some attention is given to the contribution of other disciplines to archaeology.
Prereq: ANTH 201

courses.label: ANTH 271
courses.title: Archaeological Field Methods
paras: Data gathering techniques will be studied and applied in field work on archaeological sites in the Waterioo area. Materials and transportation fee. Enrollment is limited, and instructor s permission must be obtained: Offered
concurrently with ANTH 372.
This course will meet one haif day, five days a week, for one month.

paras: This course systematically examines rasearch design and methodology in
anthropology. Prereq: ANTH 202

courses.label: ANTH 311
courses.title: Magic, Witchcraft and Religion
paras: An introduction to the way in which anthropologists study the system of behaviour and belief known as religion.

courses.title: Recent Prehistory in the Old World
paras: Cultural development from the agricul-
_ tural revolution to the rise of literacy.
Special attention to the development of agriculture as a means of subsistence and to the rise of early civilization. Areas and period of emphasis will vary from year to year.
Prereq: ANTH 201 or permission of the instructor. .
Primarily for Honours Anthroplogy students.

courses.title: Prehistoric Cultures of the Great
paras: Lakes Area ; An in depth study of the archaeological evidence of prehistoric man in the Great Lakes area from his arrival ca. 11,000 years ago to the coming of Europeans. Cultural ecology and cultural evolution will be stressed.
Prereq: ANTH 203 or consent of the instructor

courses.title: Cultural Ecology
paras: An examination of the relationships among environment, technology, society, and culture. The increasing levels of complexity will be considered in the context of hunting and foraging bands, horticultural tribes and chiefdoms, pastoral tribes and agricultural peasantry.

paras: Technology .

A general introduction to the fundamental ideas of computers. Topics treated will include the use of an interactive computing system, word processing, and the beginnings of program writing. paras: Perspective .

A study of the Psychology of Religion in its historical perspective from the nineteenth century to the present day. Methods, techniques and practices of research that are applicable to the examination of religious experience will also be introduced.

A critical study of such themes as freedom vs. happiness, nihilism, cotlectivism vs. individualism, old tablets vs. utopias, alienation, earthbound fragmentation vs. the transcendental in the artistic writings of Kafka, Brecht, Hesse, Nietzsche, Solzhenitsyn, Dostoevsky, Zamiatin, Camus, and others. Introductory Note

The core courses for each year of the Program constitute an interdisciplinary Study of Canadian problems, and are offered either in a lecture/tutorial format or @ seminar format (depending on the number of Students registered). These courses are given by faculty members of the participating departments of the University and by eminent scholars from other parts of Canada who visit the University for brief or extended periods auring the year. .

courses.label: KIN 102
courses.title: Biophysical Basis of Kinesiology
paras: Human physical movement is discussed from mechanical, anatomical and physiological viewpoints. The course provides @ generat orientation to the study of Kinesiology.

courses.label: KIN 103
courses.title: Psycho-Social Basis of Kinesiology
paras: An introduction to the study of human physical activity from psychological, sociolagical, anthropological and historical perspectives.

courses.label: KIN 116
courses.title: General and Organic Chemistry
paras: An introduction to the chemical concepts of importance in kinesiology and health studies.

courses.label: KIN 200
courses.title: Human Anatomy of the Limbs and
paras: Trunk
Functionally-oriented study of the limbs and trunk by regions using predissected cadavers. A brief introduction to Neuroanatomy is included.
Prereq: Kinesiology, Health Studies and Dance students or consent of instructor ‘
No Year 7 students are admitted.

courses.label: KIN 201
courses.title: Human Anatomy of the Brain, Head and Neck |
paras: The anatomical structure and function of the brain, cranial nerves and sense organs of the head are emphasized. Included is an introduction to. the histology of the nervous system. An opporiunity for some dissection of the head and neck is provided.
Prereq: KIN 200 or consent of instructor

courses.label: KIN 210
courses.title: Growth and Development, and Aging
paras: The physiology of human growth, development and aging is examined withspecial reference to the influence of diet, environment, exercise and disease on the normal processes. Prereq: KIN 200, BIOL 230 and 233 Cross-listed as HLTH 210..
Kinesiology

courses.label: KIN 222
courses.title: Statistical Techniques Applied to Kinesiology
paras: An introduction to descriptive and inferential statistics and the interpretation of data. A major consideration of the
‘course is the use of statistics in the solution of problems in Kinesiology and Health Studies.
Prereq: KIN and Heaith Stucies students only

courses.label: KIN 242
courses.title: Introduction to Movement Disorders
paras: An introduction to selected movement disorders and their implications for physical activity. The movement disorders examined include those which accompany neuromuscular and perceptualmotor impairment, mental retardation, cardio-vascular and ‘respiratory disease. Prereq: KIN 102 and 103

courses.label: KIN 252
courses.title: Introduction to the Sociology of Sport
paras: An introduction to the characteristics, processes and problems of sport as a social system. In addition, the social psychological aspects of sport involvement are considered. Prereq: KIN 103 and SOC 101 Cross-listed as REC 203 and SOC 348.

courses.label: KIN 255
courses.title: Introduction to Psychomotor Behaviour _
paras: An information processing approach is’ used to introduce the principles of learning and performing fine and gross motor skills. In addition, social psycho’ logical variables are studied as they relate to the facilitation or decrement in learning and performance.
Prereq: KIN 103 and PSYCH 101

courses.label: KIN 300
courses.title: Physiology of Physical Activity
paras: A study of the effects of physical activity on the muscular, circulatory and tespiratary systems and the mechanisms through which the body adapts to
‘ activity and environment.
Prereq: BIOL 230 and 233

courses.label: KIN 317
courses.title: Human Biochemistry
paras: An elementary course in human biochemistry including the metabolism and function of proteins, carbohydrates, lipids, and hormones. Emphasis is. placed onthe application of biochemical principles to human movement.
Prereq: KIN 116 or equivalent

courses.label: KIN 321
courses.title: Introduction to the Siomechanics of Human Movement
paras: Anatomical, neural and mechanical considerations in the qualitative and quantitative analysis of human movement atp examined. Concepts related to the bigstatics and, biodynamics of linked segment models of human motion are
introduced.
Prereq: PHYS 103, KIN 200 and 222

courses.label: KIN 330
courses.title: Research Design
paras: An introduction to the basic principles of scientific inquiry in Kinesiology. A systematic treatment of the logic and — practice of methods and techniques employed in research related to physical activity with an examination of design, sampling, data gathering and analysis. Prereq: KIN 222

courses.label: KIN 335
courses.title: Evaluation of Human Motor Pertormance
paras: The nature and methodology of assessment is reviewed from theoretical and empirical perspectives. Taxonomies of . motor performance are examined and principles developed for the measurement of specific constructs in field and laboratory situations. Prereq. KIN 222

courses.label: KIN 340
courses.title: Introduction to Sports Medicine
paras: An introductory course to the area of sports medicine, including the prevention, care and rehabilitation of common sports injuries. Considerable attention is directed towards the mechanisms of _ traumatic injuries as well as the management in the acute, intermediate and advanced stages of injury care. Prereq: KIN 200, 3rd and 4th year students only
* KIN 341 W 3C2L 0.5

Select Topics in Sports Medicine A course for those students wishing additional study in the area of sports medicine. Topics to be presented include trauma to the head and vertebral column, internal injuries, heat problems and the medical and non-medical use of drugs in sport.
Prereq: KIN 340

courses.label: KIN 346
courses.title: Nutrition
paras: An elementary course in nutrition with special emphasis on diet for sport and * certain physiological conditions. Cross-listed as HLTH 346.
x

courses.label: KIN 348
courses.title: Social Psychology of Health Behaviour
paras: The study and application of basic social psychological processes in relation to selected health-related behaviours (e.g. family planning, overeating, smoking, non-medical drug use, cardiovascular risk factors, patient compliance, medical care utilization).
Prereq: PSYCH 101 or consent of instructor.
Cross-listed as HLTH 348.

courses.label: KIN 349
courses.title: Principles of Behaviour Modification
paras: A course providing a general overview of behaviour modification principles and procedures. Basic principles of reinforcement, punishment, modelling and desensitization are examined as they telate to health behaviour.
Prereq: PSYCH 101 or consent of instructor
Cross-listed as HLTH 349.

courses.label: KIN 352
courses.title: Sociology of Aging
paras: An introduction to individual and popula: tion aging. Tapics discussed include: aging from an historical and comparative perspective; aging in subcultures; aging and the social structure; aging and social processes, aging and the environment; work and retirement; and aging and leisure patterns. . : Prereq: SOC 107 and one other SOC course Cross-listed as SOC 344.

courses.label: KIN 364
courses.title: Social Psychology and Physical Activity
paras: An examination of sport and other forms of physical activity as social situations. Topics such as social facilitation, modelling, person perception, expectancies, group structure, unity, motivation, leadership, conformity, and intergroup
relations are introduced in relation to
motor performance. Prereq: PSYCH 101 Cross-listed as REC 307.

courses.label: KIN 356
courses.title: Information Processing in Human Perceptual Motor Performance
paras: An information processing model of perceptual-motor behaviour is presented. Human performance theory is used to study processes mediating input and output information. Specifically, the subprocesses of storage of information in memory, perception, retrieval of information from memory and” execution of movement are examined. Prereq: KIN 222 256 »

courses.label: KIN 387
courses.title: Motor Learning
paras: A course focused on the bases and applications. of theories. of motor learning. Included are selected psychological and neurophysiotogical processes as they relate to these theories.
Prereq: KIN 222, 255

courses.label: KIN 401
courses.title: Physiological Adaptations to
paras: Physical Activity : An analysis of the physiologic adaptations that occur in response to protracted physical activity and the inftuence of such adaptations on the tesponse to work in a variety of environmental conditions. Special emphasis is given to the changes occurring in skeletal and cardiac muscles and the neuroendocrine machanisms involved.
Prereq: KIN 300 and 317

courses.label: KIN 402
courses.title: Hydrospace, Altitude and Aerospace Physiology
paras: An examination of man’s cardiorespiratory responses at rest and during work 10 selected stresses of hyperparic and hypobaric environments.
Prereq: KIN 300
- KIN 405 W 8C,2L 05 Exercise Management An examination of the rationale. and procedures used in the development of exercise programs for normally healthy individuals.
Prereq: KIN 300 and 32t

tory implications of exercise in the reha-
bilitation process. : ‘ Prereq: KIN 300 or equivaient Cross-listed as HLTH 407. .

courses.label: KIN 416
paras: Neuromuscuiar integration
An examination of the neural processes involved in the maintenance of posture and the control of movement. .
Prereq: KIN 201 or PSYCH 261 or consent of instructor

courses.label: KIN 420
courses.title: Occupational Biomechanics
paras: Biomechanical methods are applied to the study of the effect on the human operator of selected work place tasks, personal equipment, and work space | layout. Examples include the use of EMG and/or computerized models to analyse low back loading during manual lifting, the design of helmets, shoes and office chairs.
Prereq: KIN 425 (may be taken concurrently) or consent of instructor

courses.label: KIN 425B
courses.title: Biomechanics of Human Movement
paras: The quantitative measurement and ana!- ysis of the movement of the human musculo skeletal system. Multisegment dynamic movements will be studied using existing computer programs, with emphasis on kinematics, kinetics and energetics, as well as the use of EMG in the assessment of the control of the movement. Examples are presented from pathological, normal and athletic. movement.
Prereq: KIN 321

courses.label: KIN 426
courses.title: Biophysical Signal Processing and Control Systems
paras: Basic electricity and electronics required for the understanding of bioelectric recording and electrophysiology. Appiication of signal processing to biophysical signals encountered in kinesiology. Mathematical modelling of passive and active systems and the control systems (cardiac, respiratory, neuromuscular) associated with human movement. Prereq: KIN 321, KIN 300, KIN 357 or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Research Proposal
paras: An independent paper in the form of a research proposal on an approved topic. The topic may include survey, field, laboratory, theoretical, or applied research, program evaluation, mathematical modelling, fitness appraisal, etc. The format is to be determined with the supervisor and may be in chapters or in journal style. Introductory Note
Students in other disciplines may register for Optometry courses only upon the approval of the Director of the School of Optometry.

courses.label: OPTOM 100
courses.title: History and Orientation
paras: A brief history of the profession and the
_ development of visual science; a consid-
eration of legal and organizational development of optometry; the role of professional associations. ‘The role and scope of optometry and its relationship to other professions and the community.

courses.label: OPTOM 104
courses.title: Anatomy of the Eye and Associated Structures
paras: The gross, microscopic and ultra structure of ocular tissues. The embryology and comparative anatomy of the eye will be emphasized. The reiationship of the eye to the vascular supply of the head and the nervous system will be studied. This course is credited only upon completion of OPTOM 114.

courses.label: OPTOM 105
courses.title: General Pathology
paras: Basic disease processes, including inflammation, degeneration, neoplasia; pathogenic microbiology and related diseases; immunity and hypersensitivity; disease caused by physical agents; diseases of the organ systems.

courses.label: OPTOM 106
courses.title: Geometrical Optics
paras: Reflection and refraction. Image forma: tion. Optical properties of plane and curved surfaces, prisms and thin lenses. Thick lens theory and lens systems. Ray construction. Optical and ophthalmic instruments.
Prereq: PHYS 121, 121L, 122, 1221, MATH 113A/B .

courses.label: OPTOM 109
courses.title: Light and Illumination
paras: Principies of radiometry and photometry; itumination and related factors involved in the design and contro! of the visual environment in relationship to the human visual system; lighting surveys.

courses.label: OPTOM 111
courses.title: Physiological Optics
paras: The eye as an optical instrument. Ametropia and emmetropia. The refracting mechanism. The stimulus to accommodation. Ocular transmission. Visual acuity and visual performance; stray light in the eye; analysis of the retinal stimulus pattern.
Prereq: OPTOM 106

courses.label: OPTOM 114
courses.title: Anatomy of the Eye and Associated Structures
paras: A continuation of OPTOM 104 Prereq: OPTOM 104

courses.label: OPTOM 115
courses.title: General Pathology
paras: A continuation of 105. Prereq: OPTOM 105

courses.label: OPTOM 116
courses.title: Ophthalmic Optics 1
paras: Properties of optical glass and plastic, single vision lenses and prisms, lens combinations. Optics of contact lenses and clinical instruments. Ophthalmic laboratory procedures.
Prereq; OPTOM 106

courses.label: OPTOM 241
courses.title: Physiological Optics _
paras: Ocular motility, Kinematics of eye movements, muscle actions, measurements of eye movements, types of eye movements, innervational systems subserving eye movements, clinical application. Prereq: OPTOM 111

courses.label: OPTOM 242
courses.title: Clinical Optometry
paras: Lectures and laboratories on clinical techniques for examination of the optical properties of the eye.
Prereq: OPTOM 1117

courses.label: OPTOM 244
courses.title: Neurophysiology of Vision
paras: The neural processing of colour, brightness, movement and farm by the retina, lateral geniculate, cortex, superior collieulus and other brain centres. Neural Mechanisms underlying binocular depth perception, the accommedative response and eye movement.
Prereq: OPTOM 104/114

courses.label: OPTOM 245
courses.title: Ocular Pathology
paras: Signs, symptoms, clinical detection of.
primary and secondary ocular disease.
instrument techniques; record keeping.
patient counselling, referral procedures.
management of ocular emergencies.
primary health care responsibilities. Prereq: OPTOM 105/115

courses.label: OPTOM 246
courses.title: Ophthaimic Optics 2
paras: Optical problems in-bifocals, multifocals and progressive addition lenses. Lenses
for aphakics. Absorptive tenses. Aberra-
tions of thin lenses and best performance design. Optics of low vision devices.
Prereq: OPTOM 116

courses.label: OPTOM 251
courses.title: Physiological Optics
paras: The retinal stimulus pattern. Visual perception. Mach theory. Binocular vision, stereopsis, binocular integration, binocular space perception: Theory of aniseikonia. Perceptual aspects of aniseikonia. Visual illusions.
Prereq: OPTOM 241

courses.label: OPTOM 252
courses.title: Clinical Optometry
paras: Clinical techniques for the examination of thé binocular relations of the nonstrabismic patient, with particular emphasis on the study of the relationship between accommodation and convergence. Techniques of phorometry, prism vergence tests, relative accommodation tasts, reti- Nescopy, and monocular and binocular cross cylinder tests.
Prereq: OPTOM 241/242

courses.label: OPTOM 254
courses.title: Physiology of The Eye and Ocular Adnexa
paras: The physiology of the smooth muscles of the eye, the extraocular striate muscles, the lacrimal apparatus, the cornea, the iris, the lens, the ciliary body and.the vitreous body. Production and drainage of aqueous and related influ: ences on intraocular pressure. The vascular supply of the eye.
Prereq: OPTOM 104

courses.label: OPTOM 255
courses.title: Ocutar Pathology
paras: A continuation of 245 Prereq: OPTOM 245

courses.label: OPTOM 261
courses.title: Physiological Optics
paras: The perception of light. Spectral sensitivity of the eye. Photochemistry of the retina, Luminance discrimination. The Stiles-Crawford effect. Visual Acuity. intermittent stimulation. introduction to ‘colorimetry.

courses.label: OPTOM 274
courses.title: Genetics for Optometrists
paras: A brief review of Mendelian genetics, and the molecular basis of moder genetics. Inherited conditidns of particular interest, e.g., colour vision, albinism, aniridia, refractive error, retinoblastoma. Genetic counselling, and the detection _ of carriers.
Prereq: OPTOM 245

adaptation to pain, especially as they relate to cornea. The vestibular sense
_ and its influence on eyé-movements.
muscle sensory organs, including those in extra-ocular muscles, audition, olfaction, taste, visceral sensations and the
origin of headaches.

courses.label: PSYCH 120R

paras: Basic concepts and techniques of modern psychology as a behavioural science, with special emphasis on social aspects of behaviour. Topics may include the nervous system, perception, learning, memory, cognition, motivation, emotion, development, personality, social influences, psychopathology and psychotherapy.

one of PSYCH 120R or PSYCH 101
